predecessors.name: Ilkhanate
predecessors.text: Maibud (Meybod) near Yazd, where Sharaf al-Din Muzaffar was made governor

predecessors.name: Injuids
predecessors.text: Fars and Isfahan, 'the Injuid lands now fell into the hands of the Muzaffarids' (Injuids page)

successors.name: Timurid Empire
successors.text: the Muzaffarid lands after Timur's 1393 victory at Shiraz

ledger.x: 1314: Mubariz al-Din Muhammad succeeds his father Sharaf al-Din Muzaffar, governor of Maibud, and founds the Muzaffarid dynasty.
About 1319: Mubariz al-Din overthrows the atabeg of Yazd and is recognised as governor of the city by the Il-Khan government ('In around 1319 he overthrew the atabeg of Yazd').
Late 1340: Mubariz al-Din takes Kerman from the Mongol governor Qutb al-Din b.
1352: Mubariz al-Din invades Fars after the Injuids are defeated in battle ('invaded Fars in 1352... laid siege to Shiraz in 1353').
1357: Isfahan falls and Abu Ishaq is executed at Shiraz; the Injuid war ends.
1357: 'Fars was absorbed by 1357 into the expanding Muzaffarid state'; 'The Injuid lands now fell into the hands of the Muzaffarids'.
1357: Mubariz al-Din 'laid siege to that city also, and captured it in 1357'; Abu Ishaq was executed.
After 1357 the capital is Shiraz (infobox 'Kerman, Shiraz (after 1357)').
1359: Shah Shoja 'managed to occupy Azerbaijan and Arran for four months, briefly capturing Tabriz'.
1359: the four-month occupation ends; Uways returns to Tabriz.
1364: Shah Mahmud 'invaded Fars and captured Shiraz'; Shaykh Uways of the Jalayirids 'occupied Shiraz, capital of the Muzaffarid Shah Shoja, in support of his rival brother Shah Mahmud'.
1366: 'Shah Shoja would not be able to reconquer his capital until 1366'.

1374: when Shaikh Hussain Jalayir began his reign 'Tabriz was raided by the Muzaffarids'; the Muzaffarid page: after Uvais died in 1374 Shah Mahmud claimed Tabriz and 'occupied it briefly', dying the next year.
1374: the occupation of Tabriz is brief; Shah Mahmud dies 'the next year'.
1387: Timur sacks Isfahan ('a slaughter of the populace, in the Sacking of Isfahan (1387)'); Shiraz 'soon fell to Timur' and was given to Shah Yahya, and the princes rule separately until 1391.
1393: Shah Mansur loses the Battle of Shiraz to Timur and is beheaded; the remaining Muzaffarid princes swear allegiance, are received honourably and are executed ('on 22 May in Qumisha').
1393: the Muzaffarid dynasty ends with the Battle of Shiraz (1393) and the execution of its princes; infobox 'Disestablished: 1393', successor Timurid Empire.

wars.name: Muzaffarid conquest of Kerman
wars.outcome: Mubariz al-Din invades Kirman in 1339 or 1340 and holds it permanently from late 1340 after Qutb al-Din briefly retakes it with Kartid aid.

wars.name: Muzaffarid-Injuid war
wars.outcome: Abu Ishaq seeks Kirman (1347), besieges Yazd (1350-51), is defeated (1353) and executed after Isfahan falls in 1357; Fars and Isfahan pass to the Muzaffarids.

wars.name: Muzaffarid-Jalayirid wars over Azerbaijan and Shiraz
wars.outcome: Shah Shoja occupies Azerbaijan and Tabriz for four months in 1359; Uways occupies Shiraz for Shah Mahmud in 1364; Muzaffarids raid Tabriz in 1374.

wars.name: Muzaffarid civil war of Shah Shoja and Shah Mahmud
wars.outcome: Shah Mahmud, backed by the Jalayirids, holds Shiraz from 1364; Shah Shoja reconquers it in 1366.

wars.name: Sarbadar-backed revolt in Kirman
wars.outcome: 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad backs a revolt in Kirman against Shah Shuja, which fails in December 1374; Shah Mansur later sides with Amir Vali against 'Ali (1381).

wars.name: Timur's conquest of the Muzaffarids
wars.outcome: Timur sacks Isfahan (1387), decides on a campaign against Shah Mansur in 1392, reaches Shushtar and Dizful by March 1393 and wins at Shiraz in 1393; the princes are executed or sent to Samarkand.

certainty.note: A regional dynasty of cities and provinces; no treaty frontier appears on any page.
